question_text: How many people are in your household, and what are their ages?
Does anyone in the household have medical conditions requiring medication or power-dependent equipment?
What area is your home located in (city/region and neighborhood type)?
Rank these threats for your location: wildfire, earthquake, civil unrest, grid failure, water supply disruption, pandemic.
What is your primary evacuation vehicle and its current fuel range?
Where is your designated out-of-area contact, and how do they know they're your contact?
How many days of food and water do you currently have stored?
Does your generator run on propane, gasoline, or solar? What is its rated wattage?
What is your primary bug-out location and approximate distance from home?
What is your secondary bug-out location if the primary is unavailable?
What is your primary evacuation route?
What is your backup evacuation route if roads are blocked?
What are your household rally points (nearby and out-of-area)?
What communication methods will you use if cellular service fails?
What first aid capability does your household currently have?
Which prescription medications require backup stock, and for how many days?
How many gallons of potable water are stored at home right now?
What is your power backup plan during a multi-day outage?
What is currently in your 72-hour go kit for each household member?
Do you have pets, and what are their food/medication transport needs?
Which local hazards have impacted your area in the last 5 years?
How is long-term food stored (rotation method, shelf life, calories per person/day)?
What home hardening steps are already in place (fire, storm, intrusion)?
Do any household members have mobility, sensory, or cognitive support needs during emergencies?
Which household members hold current first aid/CPR or related certifications?
How confident is your household with navigation (paper maps, GPS-denied movement)?
What fire suppression and wildfire defensible-space skills do you have?
What food production skills/resources are available (garden, livestock, preservation)?
What self-defense training or tools are available, and who is trained?
How much emergency cash is accessible in small denominations?
Where are copies of IDs, insurance, property, and medical documents stored?
Which insurance policies are active and what major emergency gaps exist?
Which neighbors can be relied on for mutual aid, and for what capabilities?
What local resources are within reach (shelters, clinics, water points, HAM clubs)?
Do you have a pre-arranged mutual aid plan with friends/family/community groups?
